props.gloss_en: R' Asi: any [child] whose mother is impure by childbirth is circumcised at eight [days]
and any [child] whose mother is not impure by childbirth is not circumcised at eight
as it is said: 'a woman who conceives and bears a male shall be impure ... and on the eighth day the flesh of his foreskin shall be circumcised' (Lev 12:2-3)
Abaye: the early generations will prove it -- [the mother] was not impure by childbirth, and [the child] was circumcised at eight
one [of Rav Huna and Rav Chiyya bar Rav]: for one born by caesarean section, or one with two foreskins, one desecrates Shabbat
and the other: one does not desecrate [Shabbat for him]
they dispute only about desecrating Shabbat for him; but at eight [days] we certainly circumcise him
this depends on that: [circumcising the yotze dofen at eight] depends on the dispute about [desecrating Shabbat for him]
[R' Asi's rule] is like [a dispute of] the tannaim
the baraita: there is a home-born [slave] circumcised at one [day] and a home-born circumcised at eight; a purchased one circumcised at one and a purchased one at eight
he bought a pregnant maidservant and afterwards she gave birth: that is a purchased [slave] circumcised at eight
he bought a maidservant and her child with her: that is a purchased [slave] circumcised at one
he bought a maidservant and she conceived in his possession and gave birth: that is a home-born [slave] circumcised at eight
Rav Chama: she gave birth and afterwards he immersed her -- that is a home-born circumcised at one
he immersed her and afterwards she gave birth -- that is a home-born circumcised at eight
and the first tanna does not distinguish between immersion before or after the birth: even though his mother is not impure by childbirth, he is circumcised at eight
Rava, per R' Chama: a purchased [slave] circumcised at eight -- where he bought a pregnant maidservant, immersed her, and afterwards she gave birth
Rava, per R' Chama: a purchased [slave] circumcised at one -- where one man bought the maidservant and another her fetus
R' Yirmeya: [the first tanna's home-born circumcised at one is] one who buys a maidservant for her fetus
Rav Mesharshiya: one who buys a maidservant on condition not to immerse her
RSBG: whatever lasted thirty days, in a human, is not a נפל
as it is said: 'and their redemption, from a month old you shall redeem' (Num 18:16)
eight days, in an animal -- it is not a נפל
as it is said: 'and from the eighth day on it shall be accepted as an offering' (Lev 22:27)
hence if he did not last [thirty days], he is a doubt
Rav Adda bar Ahava: one circumcises him whichever way you take it: if he is alive, he circumcises properly; and if not, he is cutting flesh
the baraita: [a child] doubtfully of seven months, doubtfully of eight -- one does not desecrate Shabbat for him
Mar breih deRavina [with Rav Nechumei bar Zecharya]: the circumcision itself -- indeed we circumcise him
it was needed only for the preparations of circumcision, and according to R' Eliezer
the first tanna: to include the eight-month [offspring], whose slaughter does not purify it
'and if any of the animals that are yours to eat dies' (Lev 11:39) -- to include the eight-month [offspring]
R' Yosei b. R' Yehuda and R' Elazar b. R' Shimon: its slaughter purifies it
Abaye: [whether a child within thirty days is a doubtful נפל] is like [the dispute of] the tannaim [over the eight-month animal]
is it not that they dispute this: one master holds it is alive, and one holds it is dead?
Rava: rather, all agree it is dead
R' Yosei b. R' Yehuda and R' Elazar b. R' Shimon hold it is like a tereifa: is not a tereifa, though it is [as] dead, purified by its slaughter? here too, no different
and the Rabbis: it is not like a tereifa -- a tereifa had a time of fitness, this one had no time of fitness
the Rabbis do dispute RSBG
the side the first two proofs argue: the halakha does not follow RSBG [one need not wait the days]
the mishna: a calf born on a Festival may be slaughtered on the Festival
the mishna: and they agree that if it was born with its blemish, it is [counted] prepared
where it is known of it that its months [of gestation] were complete [it is no נפל]
Shmuel: the halakha follows RSBG
Abaye: [a baby within thirty days that] fell from the roof or a lion ate it -- all agree it was alive
where they dispute is where it yawned and died: one master holds it was alive, the other that it was dead
what is the practical difference? to exempt [his mother] from levirate marriage
Rav Pappa and Rav Huna b. Rav Yehoshua, served a third-born calf on its seventh day: had you waited for it until evening we would have eaten of it; now we do not eat of it
rather: where it yawned and died, all agree it was dead
where they dispute is where it fell from the roof or a lion ate it: one master holds it was dead, the other that it was alive
[the baby] died within thirty days; [Rav Dimi bar Yosef's son] sat mourning over him
a matter befell Rav Kahana within thirty days; [Rav Ashi] saw him sitting and mourning over him
Ravina in Rava's name: [the baby] died within thirty and she was betrothed -- if she is an Israelite's wife, she performs chalitza
if she is a priest's wife, she does not perform chalitza
Rav Sherevya in Rava's name: both this one and that one perform chalitza
Ravina to Rav Sherevya: in the evening Rava said so; in the morning he retracted
[Rav Sherevya:] you permitted her? may it be [His] will that you permit forbidden fat!
